items.title: Age Phenotypes, Angiographic Complexity, and Inflammatory-Metabolic Profiles in First-Presentation STEMI.
items.abstract: Age-based comparisons in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) often use a binary young-older framework, which may obscure premature non-young disease. We evaluated age-group patterns in measured modifiable risk factors, angiographic complexity, inflammatory-metabolic indices, and in-hospital outcomes in patients presenting with first STEMI. This single-center retrospective study screened 421 STEMI records between January 2019 and May 2026. After exclusions, 150 patients were selected from an eligible pool of 229 using sex-stratified, equal-size quota sampling. The groups were defined as young STEMI (≤45 years), premature non-young STEMI (men 46-55 years, women 46-65 years), and older STEMI (men >55 years, women >65 years). Measured four-component standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factor (SMuRF) burden, angiographic findings, SYNTAX score, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score (HALP), C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR), mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were analyzed. Two multivariable models were used to assess age group and SYNTAX score. Smoking prevalence decreased across groups, whereas diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and measured four-component SMuRF burden increased with age. Thrombus was most frequently observed in young STEMI. SYNTAX score, multivessel disease, SYNTAX ≥23, SII, and CAR increased with age, whereas HALP decreased. Non-smoking SMuRF burden distinguished premature non-young STEMI and older STEMI from young STEMI; older STEMI was independently associated with a higher SYNTAX score. No significant differences in mortality or MACE were detected. In this selected cohort, young STEMI was characterized by smoking predominance, a higher prevalence of angiographic thrombus, and lower coronary complexity, whereas older STEMI showed greater measured four-component SMuRF burden, increased coronary complexity, and less favorable inflammatory-metabolic indices. No differences were detected in in-hospital mortality or MACE.

Molecular basis for discrimination of cGAMP linkage isomers by a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant.
items.abstract: Riboswitches are noncoding RNA regulatory motifs predominantly found in bacteria. Signaling molecules such as c-di-GMP, c-di-AMP, and 3',3'-cGAMP have been reported to be recognized by riboswitches. In contrast, 2',3'-cGAMP functions as a second messenger in mammalian cells, yet its interaction with RNA molecules remains unclear. Here, we report the crystal structures of a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant, c-di-GMP-II-Bh, bound to 2',3'-cGAMP and 3',3'-cGAMP. Both complexes adopt a similar overall RNA scaffold with an identical binding pocket composition. However, the ligand bases adopt inverted orientations in the binding pocket, resulting in distinct interaction patterns with residues A64 and G68 and differences in base-pair stacking against the phosphodiester backbone. Structural comparison together with ligand-binding assays of structure-guided mutants using isothermal titration calorimetry reveals the molecular principles by which an RNA riboswitch discriminates among cyclic dinucleotide linkage isomers, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of RNA binding pockets to subtle ligand structural variations and provides a mechanistic framework for understanding ligand specificity in RNA-small molecule recognition.

items.title: Engineering Subcutaneous Ectopic Tertiary Lymphoid Structures as Personalized Immune-Activation Niches for Cancer Immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Tumor-associated tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) can promote anti-tumor immune responses and survival. However, intratumor TLS formation and maturation are limited in tumors with a "cold" immune phenotype, including reduced infiltration of immune cells and a suppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we present a personalized immunotherapy strategy utilizing a subcutaneously injected, bioengineered hydrogel (scTLS) that acts as an ectopic immune-activation center, effectively decoupled from the suppressive TME. Native immune cells and antigen-presenting cells (APCs) with autologous antigens are recruited through the release of chemokines. An agonist for CD40 is modified on the gel, enabling an immune-activated environment. We demonstrate that scTLSs promote robust dendritic cell (DC) activation and antigen presentation, driving the formation of organized T and B cell zones as confirmed by 3D imaging and transcriptomic analysis. This personalized, autologous vaccine-based approach elicited potent anti-tumor immune responses and effectively inhibited tumor progression across multiple murine models, with enhanced efficacy upon combination with doxorubicin-induced immunogenic cell death and immune checkpoint blockade. By overcoming the spatial and immunosuppressive limitations of the native TME, our scTLS platform offers a versatile, "off-the-shelf" engineering strategy for inducing functional TLSs to enhance therapeutic outcomes in a broad spectrum of malignancies.

items.title: Pandemic Politics: Developing Vaccines in Canada's Anti-vax Heartland.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan is a story of extremes. Through most of 2020, low case numbers, effective policy, and broad agreement among government officials, health care workers, and the public sustained a consensus that strict measures and vaccination offered the best responses; however, that consensus collapsed. The province shifted from a focal point for Canadian vaccine development to a staging ground for an anti-vaccine movement that took root on social media and then in street protests. Premier Scott Moe moved from a pro-vaccine, pro-consensus stance to a confrontational position questioning federal policies, public health measures, and vaccines. Combining traditional news sources, social media, and interviews with residents and VIDO-InterVac researchers, we track this shift. We argue that the pandemic fostered unmoderated social media discourse that overwhelmed collective responses, shaped health policies, and politicized vaccines as pro-government. Influencers inflated the movement's threat and aligned vaccine uptake to trust in science, with significant political consequences. Résumé. La pandémie de COVID-19 en Saskatchewan est une histoire marquée par les extrêmes. Pendant la majeure partie de l'année 2020, le faible nombre de cas, l'efficacité des mesures mises en place et le large consensus entre les responsables gouvernementaux, les professionnels de santé et la population ont permis de maintenir l'idée que des mesures strictes et la vaccination constituaient les meilleures réponses ; cependant, ce consensus s'est effondré. La province, qui était auparavant un pôle de référence pour le développement des vaccins au Canada, est devenue le théâtre d'un mouvement anti-vaccin qui a pris racine sur les réseaux sociaux avant de se traduire par des manifestations de rue. Le Premier ministre Scott Moe est passé d'une position favorable à la vaccination et au consensus à une posture conflictuelle remettant en cause les politiques fédérales, les mesures de santé publique et les vaccins. En combinant des sources d'information traditionnelles, les réseaux sociaux et des entretiens avec des habitants et des chercheurs du projet VIDO-InterVac, nous retraçons cette évolution. Nous soutenons que la pandémie a favorisé un discours sans modération sur les réseaux sociaux qui a pris le pas sur les réponses collectives, a façonné les politiques de santé et a politisé les vaccins en les présentant comme pro-gouvernementaux. Les influenceurs ont exagéré la menace représentée par le mouvement et ont établi un lien entre la vaccination et la confiance dans la science, ce qui a eu des conséquences politiques importantes.

items.title: RBM4 Stabilizes S100A10 mRNA to Remodel the Tumor Immune Microenvironment and Promote Immune Evasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: RNA-binding protein RBM4 regulates post-transcriptional programs, but its role in shaping the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) is unclear. We hypothesized that RBM4 enhances S100A10 mRNA stability to drive immune evasion. RBM4-S100A10 coupling was interrogated by expression profiling, RIP-qPCR, actinomycin D chase, and 3'UTR reporter assays. Gain/loss models (OE-RBM4, shS100A10) were used to assess migration/invasion and apoptosis. Immune consequences were evaluated by CD8 + T-cell co-culture (ELISA for Granzyme B, IFN-γ, TNF-α; IL-10, TGF-β) and immunofluorescence. Western blots probed cPLA2/5-LOX signaling. Subcutaneous/orthotopic models measured tumor growth, CD8 + infiltration, and effector subsets; S100A10 silencing and PD-1 blockade served as interventions. RBM4 positively correlated with S100A10 and bound the S100A10 3'UTR, increasing mRNA stability and 3'UTR-dependent reporter activity. RBM4 overexpression promoted migration/invasion and reduced apoptosis, whereas S100A10 knockdown reversed these phenotypes. In the TIME context, RBM4 reduced CD8 + T-cell effector function (lower Granzyme B/IFN-γ/TNF-α) while elevating IL-10/TGF-β, accompanied by diminished CD8 + infiltration and fewer CD8 + GZMB + /CD8 + TNF-α + cells in vivo. Mechanistically, RBM4 activated the cPLA2/5-LOX axis (increased phospho-forms with stable totals). S100A10 silencing or PD-1 blockade mitigated immune suppression and restrained tumor growth, indicating pathway specificity and therapeutic tractability. RBM4 enhances S100A10 mRNA stability, remodels the HCC TIME, suppresses CD8 + T-cell effector function, and promotes immune evasion; targeting the RBM4-S100A10 axis may improve responses to PD-1 immunotherapy.

items.title: Evaluating the Automated Extraction of Radiation Oncology Trial Data at Scale from the ClinicalTrials.gov Database Using a Large Language Model.
items.abstract: Background The rapid growth of biomedical publishing in radiation oncology has created a need for automated methods to extract structured information from unstructured text. Large language models (LLMs) show promise in biomedical natural language processing, but their use for clinical trial data curation remains to be systematically evaluated. Methods We evaluated an LLM-based extraction system for radiation oncology trials on ClinicalTrials.gov. Forty-five classification questions spanning variables such as trial design, tumor type, stage, radiotherapy modality, systemic therapy, and outcomes were implemented using the data-element-extractor Python library with three open-source LLMs (GPT-OSS-20B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Qwen-3.6-27B). A manually curated ground-truth of 94 trials was used for performance evaluation based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results Qwen-3.6-27B achieved the highest overall accuracy of 92.0% across all questions. For the 39 Boolean questions, it demonstrated 93.0% accuracy, 81.6% precision, 83.7% recall, and an F1-score of 82.6%, with 23 Boolean questions achieving an F1-score ≥80.0%. Three numerical questions reached accuracy ≥80.0%. Applied to the full dataset, the system characterized the clinical landscape of radiotherapy trials, detailing the prevalence of advanced techniques (e.g., 13.7% SBRT) and the integration of systemic agents, including chemotherapy (57.3%) and immunotherapy (26.1%). Conclusion LLM-based extraction can enable accurate, scalable curation of radiotherapy trial data. While challenges remain with complex categorical or numerical variables, open-source LLMs can serve as effective components of transparent, auditable clinical research pipelines.

items.title: Vaccines targeting the inflammasome protein ASC reduce inflammation and downstream pathology in multiple disease models.
items.abstract: The inflammasome is an innate immune complex responsible for aberrant interleukin-1β (IL-1β) signaling in numerous chronic inflammatory diseases, including gout and Alzheimer's disease. The inflammasome is composed of several proteins, including the apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain (ASC). We developed vaccines targeting various regions of ASC using a Qβ virus-like particle (VLP) platform to assess the efficacy of anti-ASC antibodies for inhibiting inflammasome activity. Using a mouse model of gout, we assessed seven vaccines targeting mouse ASC for their ability to reduce inflammasome activation and neutrophil responses. Three vaccines targeting different regions of the ASC protein (pyrin domain, linker region, and the caspase activation and recruitment domain) successfully targeted ASC, reduced IL-1β, and reduced neutrophil activation. Combining these three vaccines into one cocktail vaccine yielded similar efficacy in the gout model with a favorable safety profile. The combined ASC vaccine also reduced inflammasome levels and pathologically phosphorylated tau in a transgenic mouse model of tauopathy and did not significantly impair host immune responses to bacterial or viral infections. Thus, Qβ-VLP vaccines against ASC can neutralize pathological inflammasome activity across multiple inflammatory disease models.

items.title: Selection and Management of Patients With Resectable Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer Receiving Perioperative FLOT: A Modified Delphi Consensus Approach.
items.abstract: Perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) is a guideline-recommended standard for patients with resectable gastric cancer or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma globally. Guidance is limited on patient selection, nutritional optimization, and toxicity management within existing guidelines. This study aimed to develop an international consensus to address these management gaps. A modified Delphi methodology, informed by the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method, was conducted virtually between March and August 2025. A multidisciplinary panel of 16 experts independently rated draft clinical statements across multiple domains. Responses were anonymized, with structured, iterative rounds of feedback and re-rating. Consensus was defined a priori as a median score of 7-9 (appropriate) or 1-3 (inappropriate) with a disagreement index ≤1.0. Consensus was reached on 66.3% of the statements. Experts agreed that patients aged >70 years should not be routinely excluded from perioperative FLOT but require comprehensive assessment; inclusion of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) 0-1 is appropriate, and ECOG PS 0-2 may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Adequate organ function, correction of baseline conditions, hepatitis B screening, and dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase testing are appropriate before FLOT initiation. Universal baseline nutritional screening and support, proactive intervention for malnourished patients, and structured physical activity were endorsed. Surgical planning was supported through multidisciplinary input, with defined perioperative windows, individualized dosing, and flexibility in pre-/postoperative cycles. For toxicity management, the panel supported dose modification over drug omission, where possible. This Delphi consensus provides expert-driven, practice-oriented advisories codifying fitness-based selection, nutrition-forward optimization, and pragmatic toxicity management. The resulting guidance builds on current standards and provides internationally applicable consensus statements to ultimately enhance patient care.

items.title: In vitro antiviral activity of the RdRp inhibitor 4'-fluorouridine against a porcine teschovirus clinical isolate.
items.abstract: Porcine Teschovirus (PTV) is an economically significant swine pathogen with a global distribution that can cause severe neurological, respiratory, and reproductive diseases. However, no specific vaccines or antiviral drugs are currently available. To address the absence of specific antiviral therapies for PTV, this study aimed to identify a clinically promising antiviral candidate through in vitro compound screening. We began by isolating and purified a contemporary PTV strain (PTV/Shandong/2024) from a clinical swab of a dead piglet. We also established a strain-specific RT-qPCR assay to accurately quantify PTV RNA load. A subsequent targeted screen of a hepatitis C virus (HCV) inhibitor library identified the nucleoside analog 4'-fluorouridine (4'-FLU) as a potent inhibitor of PTV replication in vitro. Treatment with 4'-FLU significantly reduced viral load and cytopathic effects in infected PK-15 cells. The compound exhibited potent antiviral activity, with a half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) of 1.234 µM, and low cytotoxicity, with a half maximal cytotoxic concentration (CC₅₀) of 295.7 µM. This resulted in a high selectivity index of 239.6, indicating a wide therapeutic window. Time-of-addition experiments revealed that 4'-FLU acts primarily during the early stages of viral replication. These results provide the first evidence that 4'-FLU suppresses PTV replication in vitro supporting its further evaluation as a candidate antiviral against PTV.

items.title: Distinct immune signatures define hepatitis D- versus hepatitis B-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized. In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108). Plasma levels of 92 soluble inflammatory mediators (SIMs) were quantified using proximity extension assay in HCC patients [HBV-HCC (n=50), HDV-HCC (n=30), and matched non-HCC controls (HBV=19, HDV=17)]. At the time of HCC diagnosis, patients with CHD were younger, had more impaired liver synthesis and detoxification function, and lower levels of AST, CRP, and leukocytes. HDV-HCCs presented with smaller tumors, less frequent portal vein infiltration, and more often fulfilled Milan criteria (all p<0.01). Systemic immune profiling revealed distinct inflammatory patterns between both etiologies. Compared with HBV-HCC, HDV-HCC was characterized by a comparatively stronger IL-10-associated immunoregulatory signature, whereas HBV-HCC exhibited a more pronounced pro-inflammatory profile involving IL-6- and phosphorylation- and proliferation-associated signaling. Despite these differences, event-free survival did not differ between groups. HBV-HCC more frequently presented with advanced tumor stage, whereas HDV-HCC was associated with more severe underlying liver disease but smaller tumors. Importantly, HBV-associated and HDV-associated HCC exhibit distinct systemic inflammatory signatures, potentially reflecting differences in systemic immune regulation between etiologies. These findings may have implications for biomarker development and future etiology-specific therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Inter-α-inhibitor heavy chain 4 levels in incident and prevalent patients with primary biliary cholangitis.
items.abstract: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is an autoimmune liver disease characterised by progressive bile duct injury. We recently showed that inter-α-inhibitor heavy chain 4 (ITIH4) levels are elevated in patients with PBC. Here, we investigated the potential of ITIH4 as a biomarker for disease severity and treatment response. We included 237 patients with primary biliary cholangitis, 80 incident (newly diagnosed), 157 prevalent (with established disease) and 100 healthy controls. All patients were followed for 12 months during initiation or continuation of ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA). Associations with treatment response, patient type, autoimmune hepatitis (AIH-PBC) and sex were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. The prognostic value of baseline ITIH4 for following response was assessed using logistic regression. ITIH4 levels were significantly higher in both PBC cohorts compared with healthy controls (incident: 274 µg/ml, prevalent: 283 µg/ml, controls: 221 µg/ml; p   p  = .003, p  = .034 and p  = .013). Correlations between ITIH4 and markers of disease severity were generally weak. Baseline ITIH4 was not significantly associated with treatment response (OR 0.994, p  = .14). ITIH4 was consistently elevated in patients with PBC compared with healthy individuals. Baseline ITIH4 levels did not independently predict response and correlations with established severity markers remained weak. These findings do not support its use as a prognostic marker or as an addition to existing clinical biomarkers.

items.title: Clinical Risk Factors for Advanced Fibrosis in Pathology-Proven Steatotic Liver Disease: Emphasis on Nonelder Subjects.
items.abstract: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) may lead to advanced liver diseases. We aimed to identify clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis in pathology-proven SLD patients in a hepatitis B virus (HBV) endemic population, with emphasis on nonelder subjects. Adult SLD patients diagnosed via pathology at National Taiwan University Hospital between June 2009 and December 2023 were recruited. Advanced fibrosis was defined as F2 to F4 fibrosis. Patients were stratified by age (< 50 years defined as nonelder), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and HBV infection. Clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis and at-risk steatohepatitis were investigated, and the predictive performance of noninvasive scores was examined. Among 223 pathology-proven SLD patients, older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.04), alcohol consumption (OR: 5.77), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (OR: 2.13), chronic HBV infection (OR: 2.52), and obesity (OR: 2.64) were independent risk factors for advanced fibrosis. In the nonelder subgroup, older age (OR: 1.10) and obesity (OR: 3.75) were significant. In the MASLD subgroup, older age (OR: 1.04), hypertension (OR: 2.31), T2DM (OR: 3.07), and chronic HBV infection (OR: 3.59) remained significant. Obesity (OR: 4.14) was a significant risk factor for at-risk steatohepatitis in the nonelder subgroup. NAFLD fibrosis score had the highest AUROC (0.724) for advanced fibrosis in the entire cohort, while FIB-4 performed best in nonelder subjects. Older age, alcohol, T2DM, chronic HBV infection, and obesity were associated with advanced fibrosis. Risk factors and noninvasive score performance varied in nonelder subjects.

items.title: Dosimetric impact of baseline shift plan in a magnetic resonance linear accelerator according to target motion and plan characteristics.
items.abstract: In this study, the dosimetric effect of baseline shift (BLS) in a magnetic resonance linear accelerator was investigated and compared with adapt-to-position (ATP), adapt-to-shape (ATS), and an uncorrected plan without adaptation. In a simulation dataset consisting of 30 patients (10 prostate, 10 liver, 10 pancreatic), all structures were rigidly shifted by 1, 3, 5, and 10 mm separately in the superior-inferior and posterior directions, and four plans (ATS reoptimization, ATP reoptimization, BLS using the segment aperture morphing algorithm, and an uncorrected plan without adaptation) were generated for each shift condition. Planning target volume (PTV) coverage and PTV maximum dose (Dmax) were then compared. The dosimetric effects of BLS on the targets and organs at risk (OARs) under non-rigid anatomic changes were also evaluated using a clinical dataset based on magnetic resonance imaging acquired during treatment. In the simulation analysis of superior-inferior shifts, target coverage using BLS was comparable to that using ATS and ATP across all disease sites and improved compared with that using the uncorrected plan. For posterior shifts, target coverage remained comparable to that using ATS and ATP; however, BLS increased the PTV Dmax at all posterior shift magnitudes (1-10 mm) in prostate and pancreatic cases, with limited increases in liver cases. In the clinical dataset, OAR doses upon left-right or anterior-posterior displacement were greater using BLS than using ATP, ATS, and uncorrected plans in the prostate and pancreatic cases, with limited increases in the liver cases. The dosimetric impact of BLS relies on motion direction and plan characteristics. BLS was stable for superior-inferior shifts, whereas posterior shifts may increase PTV hotspots and OAR doses. Therefore, clinical application of BLS should consider motion direction and plan design rather than applying a uniform strategy.
items.journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

items.title: Site-Specific Outcomes and Genomics in Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Clinical and molecular features of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) according to involved metastatic sites have not been well characterized. We used the Foundry platform to query information for patients with metastatic PDAC at MD Anderson Cancer Center. Involved metastatic sites were extracted using natural language processing from imaging reports and verified by chart reviews. Overall survival (OS) and next generation sequencing (NGS) data were analyzed. In a cohort of 1,095 patients (median overall survival [OS]: 22.8 months), lung-only metastasis was associated with longer median OS (57.6 months, p<0.0001). Patients with metastases not involving the liver had OS of 41.3 months, while liver-only (19.5 months) and multiple sites including liver (19.3 months) had the poorest survival. TP53 mutation rates were higher in liver-involved groups (84-85%) versus lung-only (73%) and non-liver metastases (67%, p<0.0001). Lower rates of GNAS mutations were detected in liver-only (5%) and liver-involved (2%) cases, higher in lung-only (8%) and non-liver (10%, p<0.01). The frequency of KRAS mutation and mutant allele distribution were not significantly different in tissue based NGS. However, in liquid biopsy analysis (n = 240), lung-only metastasis showed the lowest mutation detection (50%), TP53 (23%) and KRAS (10%), compared to liver-only detection rates of 65%, 46%, and 52% respectively (p values: 0.009, 0.02, <0.001). Patients with PDAC without liver metastasis have significantly improved OS and lower rates of TP53 mutation. Patients with lung-only metastasis had longer OS, a lower liquid-biopsy positivity rate, and a lower rate of KRAS detection by liquid biopsy; because liquid biopsy may under-detect KRAS in lung-only disease, tumor-tissue sequencing should be prioritized in these patients as KRAS-directed therapies emerge.

items.title: Mapping Perioperative Vulnerability and Optimization in Hepatectomy: A Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis of Sarcopenia, Frailty, and Prehabilitation.
items.abstract: Risk assessment before hepatectomy is no longer based only on tumor burden, liver function, and technical resectability. Muscle status, frailty, nutrition, exercise capacity, and prehabilitation are now discussed more often in this setting. This study reviewed how these topics appear in the hepatectomy literature and how they relate to the more established body composition literature. Relevant publications were retrieved from the Science Citation Index Expanded of the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace (version 6.4.R1), VOSviewer (version 1.6.20), and RStudio (version 2025.05.1 + 513) were used to analyze publication trends, collaboration networks, journal distributions, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence, citation bursts, and temporal patterns. A total of 498 publications were included. Publication output increased during the study period, especially after 2021. Japan, China, and the United States contributed the most papers, whereas several European countries had stronger positions in the collaboration network. Sarcopenia and body composition remained the main basis of this literature. Frailty, functional vulnerability, nutritional support, exercise, and prehabilitation appeared more often in recent years, but collaboration between institutions and author groups was still incomplete. Current hepatectomy research in this area is still centered on body composition-based risk assessment. Newer studies have added frailty, functional reserve, nutrition, exercise capacity, and prehabilitation to the same perioperative discussion. Future work should test practical pathways that connect these measures with surgical decision-making, patient selection, and preoperative optimization.

items.title: Effectiveness of prenatal predictors for congenital diaphragmatic hernia on survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation requirement: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound (USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital (BWC). CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve (AUC) calculated. 91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge. O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and for right and complex left CDH is required.

items.title: Lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) regulates macrophage plasticity and immune checkpoint expression in colorectal liver metastases.
items.abstract: Colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) are a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer and are characterised by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in which tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) play a central role. However, the molecular mechanisms driving TAM plasticity and maintenance remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated macrophage heterogeneity in CRLM and examined the contribution of the epigenetic regulator lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) to TAM polarisation. Analysis of patient-derived specimens by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and transcriptional profiling identified a population of large TAMs (L-TAMs) enriched in the peritumoral niche that displayed an immunosuppressive, M2-like phenotype and was associated with poor clinical outcome. In contrast, smaller TAMs (S-TAMs) exhibited a more inflammatory transcriptional programme, including increased IL1β expression. Tumour-conditioned media reproduced these distinct macrophage phenotypes in vitro, indicating that tumour-derived factors actively shape TAM identity. Pharmacological inhibition of LSD1 using baicalin or INCB059872 reduced the expression of CD206 and the immune checkpoint molecule PD-L1, consistent with macrophage reprogramming away from a tumour-promoting state. Collectively, these findings identify LSD1 as an epigenetic regulator of macrophage plasticity in CRLM, implicated in the maintenance of immunosuppressive TAM phenotypes, and potentially able to induce phenotypic reversion. Our findings identify LSD1 as a regulator of TAM phenotype and support further investigation of LSD1 targeting as a strategy to remodel the metastatic tumour microenvironment and potentially enhance anti-tumour immunity.
